task.description:
Implement the design at lib/letflow/design/iss0451-poller-crash-budget-isolation.md exactly as specified (it passed CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's gate after 2 rework cycles, both of which found and fixed real OTP-semantics defects -- the design has been independently re-verified live, twice, so implement it as written rather than second-guessing its mechanism choices; if you find a genuine additional defect while implementing, stop and report it rather than silently deviating).

Summary of what the design requires (read the design doc itself for the authoritative, complete spec -- this is a pointer, not a restatement):
1. A new module Letflow.Supervisor.PollersBreaker (circuit breaker GenServer) at lib/letflow/supervisor/pollers_breaker.ex, per the design's state machine (:closed/:open/:half_open), monitoring Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers, trip threshold, exponential backoff schedule, and Supervisor.start_child/2-based restart mechanism (NOT restart_child/2 -- the design explicitly corrected this).
2. lib/letflow/application.ex's children list: Pollers' entry changed to Supervisor.child_spec(Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers, restart: :temporary) used directly as the list entry, PollersBreaker added as a new child listed after Pollers and before Http, and the top-level Supervisor.start_link/2 opts' max_restarts raised per the design's stated value.
3. test/letflow/supervisor/pollers_test.exs's existing restart_pollers!/0 helper (or whatever the design calls it) needs updating from terminate_child+restart_child to terminate_child+start_child/2 with the full child spec, per the design's own §5/§6 discussion of this consequence -- this is a required correction to EXISTING test code, not new test authoring (TEST-DESIGNER handles the NEW persistent-fault regression test at the next step; you fix this specific existing-test breakage since it's a structural consequence of your own application.ex/pollers.ex changes, not new coverage).

After implementing: run `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` and `mix format --check-formatted` and fix anything either flags. Run the EXISTING test/letflow/supervisor/ test files (pollers_test.exs, infrastructure_test.exs, http_test.exs) and confirm they still pass under your changes -- REQ-219's own AC2/AC4 tests living in pollers_test.exs must not regress (per ISS-0451's own AC3). Do NOT write the new persistent-fault regression test yourself -- that is TEST-DESIGNER's job at the next step; you may leave a TODO comment or simply leave it to that step.

This will then go to SECURITY-REVIEWER (supervision-tree/boot-sequence changes are in scope even though this isn't a tenant-data path -- confirm scope test yourself and state your reasoning either way) and REVIEWER (OTP idiom, supervision integrity) before TEST-DESIGNER.
acceptance_criteria: lib/letflow/supervisor/pollers_breaker.ex created, matching the design's module/state/callback spec
lib/letflow/application.ex updated per the design (child spec syntax, PollersBreaker added, max_restarts value)
test/letflow/supervisor/pollers_test.exs's restart helper corrected to use start_child/2, not restart_child/2, per the design's own required consequence
test/letflow/supervisor/pollers_test.exs, infrastructure_test.exs, http_test.exs all still pass (REQ-219 AC2/AC4 no regression, per ISS-0451 AC3)
No new persistent-fault regression test written by this step -- that is TEST-DESIGNER's job next

result.summary: Implemented all three required changes per the design exactly as specified: (1) new Letflow.Supervisor.PollersBreaker GenServer at lib/letflow/supervisor/pollers_breaker.ex, matching the design's :closed/:open/:half_open state machine, backoff schedule (1s/5s/30s/2m/5m cap), 2s observation window, Supervisor.start_child/2-based restart mechanism (never restart_child/2), and breaker_state/0 accessor; (2) lib/letflow/application.ex's children list changed to Supervisor.child_spec(Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers, restart: :temporary) as a direct list entry, PollersBreaker added after Pollers/before Http, top-level max_restarts raised 3->5 (max_seconds stays 5); (3) test/letflow/supervisor/pollers_test.exs's restart_pollers!/0 helper corrected from terminate_child+restart_child to terminate_child+start_child/2 with the full child spec, made tolerant of {:error, {:already_started, pid}} since PollersBreaker can win a restart race against this helper too. mix compile --warnings-as-errors: clean (0 warnings). mix format --check-formatted: clean. infrastructure_test.exs (updated for the new 4th top-level child, PollersBreaker) and http_test.exs: 6/6 pass, every run. pollers_test.exs: 3 of its 4 tests pass every run; its 'AC4: crash-loop isolation' test is FLAKY -- it passed in 3 of 5 --seed-varied runs and failed with a MatchError in the other 2 (see result.issues for the root cause, which is a genuine design gap, not an implementation bug). Reported as FAIL per this step's own task instructions ('confirm they still pass... REQ-219's own AC2/AC4 tests... must not regress') since AC2/AC4 coverage is not reliably green -- not silently patched into a passing-but-unrepresentative shape. STOPPED here per the task's own 'if you find a genuine additional defect, stop and report' instruction rather than redesigning the existing AC4 test's semantics myself, since fixing it correctly requires a design-level decision (see result.issues) that CODE-DESIGNER/REVIEWER should make, not one I should make unilaterally while implementing.

issues.title: Design doc §5's guidance for updating pollers_test.exs's existing AC4 test does not produce a deterministic test once Letflow.Supervisor.PollersBreaker is live -- a genuine, previously-unflagged two-restarter race, empirically reproduced (fails ~40% of --seed-varied runs)
issues.detail: lib/letflow/design/iss0451-poller-crash-budget-isolation.md §5's 'Second, previously-unflagged consequence' section instructs updating pollers_test.exs's manual terminate_child+restart_child call sites (including the AC4 test's own inline manual-restart step, lines ~116-119 as read for the design) to terminate_child+start_child/2, and says the test's crash-loop procedure must 'expect Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers to be restarted via PollersBreaker's own :DOWN handler... instead of asserting a bare top-level automatic restart occurred.' Implementing this literally (test/letflow/supervisor/pollers_test.exs, AC4 test body) surfaces a race the design did not anticipate: Letflow.Supervisor.PollersBreaker ALSO monitors Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers and reacts to the SAME terminate_child/2-induced :DOWN this test relies on to force init/1 to re-read its env overrides -- concurrently with whatever the test process does next. Two failure modes, both empirically reproduced during implementation: (a) if the test issues its own start_child/2 call for the freshly-terminated Pollers (the design's literal instruction), it races PollersBreaker's own start_child/2 call for the identical :temporary child spec -- whichever call loses gets {:error, {:already_started, pid}} instead of {:ok, pid}, a MatchError against the design's own literal {:ok, pid} = ... pattern. Reproduced deterministically with --seed 0, and flakily (2 of 5 runs) with varied seeds. (b) If the test instead removes its own competing start_child/2 call and waits for the breaker's restart (an alternative I tried and then reverted, since it does not preserve the original AC4 semantics either), Letflow.Scheduler.Poller's zero-delay first tick means the breaker-restarted Pollers can already be crash-looping, inside the breaker's own 2-second observation window, before the test process is even scheduled to run its next line -- there is no synchronous window left (unlike the ORIGINAL top-level-auto-restart mechanism this test was written against) for the test to clear :force_poller_crash before a second exhaustion cycle occurs; empirically the breaker reached :open (consecutive_trips: 2) before the test's post-wait assertions ran, so Process.whereis(Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers) was nil, not a stable third pid. Root cause: PollersBreaker's restart of Pollers is fundamentally asynchronous relative to the test process (a Process.monitor :DOWN message + handle_info dispatch + a synchronous but still message-passing-mediated start_child/2 call), whereas the ORIGINAL test relied on the test process's OWN synchronous terminate_child+restart_child call completing strictly before control returned to it -- a property that held for the top-level Supervisor's restart call but does not carry over to a race between the test process and a third, independently-scheduled GenServer both trying to restart the same :temporary child in reaction to the same underlying event.
issues.recommendation: This needs a design-level decision, not a test-only patch: either (1) give PollersBreaker a way to ignore a :DOWN it did not itself expect to be racing a test-initiated restart against (e.g. a test-only synchronization hook, double-gated like pollers_init_probe/force_poller_crash, that lets a test coordinate with the breaker's :closed-state handler before triggering its own terminate_child), or (2) redefine the AC4 test's own procedure to not attempt a manual pre-restart at all and instead drive the entire scenario (healthy Pollers -> crash flag set -> terminate -> breaker's restart -> crash-loop -> breaker's own exhaustion-detection -> :open -> :half_open recovery once the flag is cleared) as a single breaker-mediated flow matching ISS-0451's OWN new regression test's shape (design doc §6.2) rather than trying to preserve the original single-top-level-restart AC4 test's exact structure, or (3) some other mechanism CODE-DESIGNER/REVIEWER judges better. Left implemented as the design's literally-specified start_child/2 call (failure mode (a)) in the current test/letflow/supervisor/pollers_test.exs rather than the (b) workaround, since (a) is the more direct, more clearly design-traceable illustration of the race for whoever picks this up next.

result.next_action: Route back to CODE-DESIGNER (not SECURITY-REVIEWER/REVIEWER) to resolve the pollers_test.exs AC4-test race documented in result.issues[0] -- a design-level decision is needed before this can proceed to the normal SECURITY-REVIEWER/REVIEWER gate sequence, since the currently-implemented production code (pollers_breaker.ex, application.ex) is believed correct and complete per the design and is not itself in question; only the existing AC4 test's adaptation is unresolved.
